title: CON-quest. II. Spatially and spectrally resolved HCN/HCO<SUP>+</SUP> line ratios in local luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxies
question: Reveal the distributions of HCN and HCO+ J=3-2 emission in local U/LIRGs and investigate whether and how their line ratios relate to galaxy properties, AGN strength, excitation conditions, and outflows/inflows.

data.sensitivity: 0.145 to 0.730 mJy beam^-1 in 20 km s^-1 channels

what.value: Bolometric AGN fraction (alpha_AGN) from Spitzer/IRS spectroscopic data and [N II]122/[O III]88 line fluxes

evidence.quote: For the bolometric AGN fraction, we employed the relative AGN contribution to the bolometric total luminosity calculated by Díaz-Santos et al. (2017) based on Spitzer /IRS spectroscopic data.

For the elemental N/O ratio, we used the far-infrared fine-structure line ratio of [N ii] 122 /[O iii] 88 (calculated from galaxy-integrated line fluxes; taken from Díaz-Santos et al. 2017) as a rough estimator.

what.value: Visual merger stage classification based on Spitzer/IRAC 3.6 um images

evidence.quote: For the merger stage, we adopted the visual classification by Stierwalt et al. (2013) based on Spitzer /IRAC 3.6 µm images.

what.value: CON classification based on HCN-vib surface density

evidence.quote: The existence of a CON is based on the HCN-vib surface density measured by Paper I.

recipe.goal: Extract resolved and global spectra and generate moment maps
recipe.method: Extract spectra from a synthesized-beam-sized aperture ('resolved') and a 10x10 beam elliptical aperture ('global') centered on each galaxy's kinematic center; integrate over visually determined velocity ranges to create moment 0 (no clipping) and moment 1 and 2 maps (3-sigma clipping).
key_parameters: Resolved aperture = 1x1 beam; Global aperture = 10x10 beam; 3-sigma threshold clipping for moment 1 and 2; velocity integration ranges from ±150 to ±500 km s^-1 (Table 3)
assumptions: No correction for line blending/overlapping; for IRAS 17578-0400, continuum levels of 0.02 Jy (resolved) and 0.07 Jy (global) assumed

recipe.goal: Calculate line luminosities and global/resolved HCN/HCO+ line ratios, and correlate with galaxy properties
recipe.method: Compute L'_HCN and L'_HCO+ using Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005) formula; fit power-law relations with L_IR; compute L'_HCN/L'_HCO+ ratios and test correlations with alpha_AGN, L_AGN^bol, L_IR, SFR, S60/S100, and [N II]122/[O III]88 using Spearman rank correlation with Monte Carlo perturbation and bootstrapping.
key_parameters: Excluded non-detected galaxies (UGC 11763, UGC 2982, NGC 5734) from correlation analysis; 12 galaxies used for [N II]122/[O III]88
assumptions: L_bol = 1.15 L_IR; SFR = (1 - alpha_AGN) x 10^-10 L_IR (Chabrier IMF)

recipe.goal: Spatially and spectrally resolved (pixel-by-pixel and spaxel-by-spaxel) line ratio analysis in ppV space
recipe.method: Compute L'_HCN/L'_HCO+ on a pixel-by-pixel basis (spectral integration then 3-sigma clipping) and spaxel-by-spaxel basis (3-sigma clipping on both cubes), extract statistical percentiles, and visualize spaxels exceeding the 90th percentile in 3D position-position-velocity (ppV) space.
key_parameters: Pixel size = 0.05'' x 0.05''; spaxel size = 0.05'' x 0.05'' x 20 km s^-1; clipping = 3-sigma; structure threshold = 90th percentile

recipe.goal: Non-LTE radiative transfer modeling of excitation conditions
recipe.method: Run one-zone non-LTE radiative transfer calculations using RADEX with uniform sphere LVG geometry to predict L'_HCN/L'_HCO+ as a function of H2 volume density across grids of T_kin, N_H2, X_HCN, and electron abundance X_e-.
assumptions: Uniform sphere geometry with LVG; HCO+ electron collisional rate coefficients for J>=3 scaled by dipole moment squared (mu^2) from HCN rates

recipe.method: Run two-phase (pre-shock and post-shock) time-dependent gas-grain chemical models using the C-shock module of UCLCHEM to track gas temperature, density, and fractional abundances of HCN, HCO+, and electrons as a function of post-shock time.
key_parameters: Pre-shock: n_H2 = 10^3 cm^-3, T = 10 K, A_V = 2 mag, radiation field = 1 Habing, cosmic-ray ionization rate = 1.3 x 10^-17 s^-1, duration = 10^5 yr; Post-shock: v_shock = 10, 20, 30, 40 km s^-1
assumptions: Standard Galactic elemental abundances; constant radiation field and cosmic-ray ionization rate during shock

score_reason: The paper provides comprehensive tables of target coordinates, beam sizes, channel sensitivities, velocity integration ranges, aperture definitions, and exact numerical answer keys for all 23 galaxies, alongside clear parameter sets for RADEX and UCLCHEM; only minor imaging/uvcontsub channel details are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The two ALMA datasets (2017.1.00759.S and 2018.1.01344.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the imaging and aperture extraction recipes are straightforward (natural weighting, 20 km/s channels, 1x1 and 10x10 beam apertures), and Tables 3, 4, 5, and 6 provide complete numeric benchmarks.
